title: intentd's watcher arms go red inside the release gate right after the workspace build and pass alone at the same load
body:
intentd's watcher arms fail inside the release gate right after the full workspace build, and pass alone at the same load.

**Measured 2026-09-19** on the 3.1.0 cut. Six arms went red twice in `dvb build release`'s cargo gate on identical intentd bytes at a one-minute load under 10: `the_daemon_lists_the_project_registry::a_project_added_to_the_registry_is_listed_without_a_restart`, `daemon_watch::one_external_edit_costs_a_bounded_number_of_ingests`, `daemon_watch::a_change_to_a_path_outside_the_sync_scope_drives_no_ingest`, `daemon_watch::an_external_edit_reaches_the_store_with_nobody_running_sync`, `daemon_watch::a_burst_of_edits_is_debounced_into_far_fewer_ingests`, `a_source_edit_reaches_the_index_and_costs_canon_nothing`. Every panic is a watcher wait expiring (ten seconds of polling for the registry arm, `ATTEMPTS` of `PAUSE` for daemon_watch). Alone, in a private worktree at the same HEAD under the gate's environment at load 5, intentd's suite passed 38 of 39, the one red the ruled flake a_daemon_outlives_nobody. The gate runs these arms seconds after building every workspace test target and running intent-cli's suite, and its once-only intentd re-run two minutes later passed on every run where it fired.

**What this is not:** a watcher defect. What it is: arms whose delivery windows assume an FSEvents pipeline that has nothing queued, on a host where a workspace build has just written tens of thousands of files.

**The ask:** either the arms wait for the watcher to acknowledge its first event before the timed wait begins, or the gate runs intentd's suite last, after the filesystem has settled, and the driver's family list (`4da3ca19d`) stops being the thing that decides. M. The records are vc's scratchpad `release-red-1.md` and the gate logs `intent-release-gates.kwRZAG3elO` and `.4sA17TkSWL` of 2026-09-19.



**Landed, not closed** (2026-09-19, in the commit that carries this paragraph, patch-id b654c01e7, test-only). Option (A) as ruled: each of the six arms first writes a sentinel (a thread file, a source file, or a registry entry) and waits up to `ARM_ATTEMPTS` (`ATTEMPTS * 12`, counted in tries, never a clock) for the watcher to act on it, and only then starts its own bounded wait. Two cold gate-shaped runs, each `cargo build -p intentd && cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` in a private worktree: with (A), load 14.66 at the start, the workspace 0 failed (intent-cli 321 + 1 + 716, intentd 9 + 5 + 39, intentsvcs 297 + 1510, testkit 9), all six arms green; the CONTROL on the unfixed base, load 70.38, also 0 failed with all six arms green. So that instrument does not reproduce the red, and these runs show (A) breaks nothing, not that it fixes anything. **Closing condition:** the next real `dvb build release` gate passes all six arms first time. The driver's load-sensitive family list stays as it is until then.


**The closing condition's load clause** (vc, 2026-09-20, clock read 13:20Z; from ic's reading of the arms in its sync before vc's fold d7fce1a76 and its drive of all six after it, dc's read-only walk over the live channel received between vc's clock reads of 13:14Z and 13:16Z, and cc's load measurement; every citation below re-read by vc in the main checkout at HEAD d7fce1a76). The six-arm pass counts only for a gate run whose host load was read at the floor, about 10 on this host, and the run that closes this issue records that load beside its verdict. Why: load reds an arm that asserts something DID happen and never false-greens it (cc ran 0488+0489's whole suites green at load 592 and again at 90, the difference wall-clock only), and that inverts for an assertion that NOTHING happened within a window, where slowness and the asserted absence are the same observation. Five of the six arms carry at least one such assertion: `the_daemon_lists_the_project_registry.rs:62` (`!found.watched && found.dispatched == 0`, asserted the instant the listing is found, no window); `daemon_watch.rs:235` (`(1..=3).contains(&cost)`, whose `<= 3` half is the absence) and `daemon_watch.rs:244` (`assert_eq!(ingested, resting)` after a raw `for _ in 0..STABLE_FOR { sleep(PAUSE) }`); `daemon_watch.rs:296` (the same equality after the same raw loop, and it is the whole subject of `a_change_to_a_path_outside_the_sync_scope_drives_no_ingest`; its positive control proves the watch is alive, not that the window was long enough); `daemon_watch.rs:343` (`ingests < WRITES`, which load pushes green from the other side, since more coalescing means fewer ingests); `a_source_edit_reaches_the_index_and_costs_canon_nothing.rs:123` (`assert_eq!(ingested, before)` the instant the index presence is seen, with no settle between them, so a canon ingest that merely lags the index one reads as a pass). The one arm with no such assertion is `daemon_watch::an_external_edit_reaches_the_store_with_nobody_running_sync`, sound at any load. It is a class and not six coincidences because `settle()` was hardened on the presence path alone (quiet is the count stopping, never a duration), while every absence assertion sits behind a raw fixed-duration sleep or behind nothing. This corrects forward the first two readings: ic's 13:13Z sync named one bound in one arm, and dc's walk confined the class to daemon_watch.rs, which the source-edit arm's own file disproves. The 0481 arming (option (A)) is presence-asserting and stands; it covers the first event's backlog and says nothing about the bounds that run after it. No arm changes now (hv, 2026-09-20: no testing tests, no yak-shaving); the arms are sound at the floor, and nobody has audited beyond these six: dc's walk cleared intentsvcs and intent-cli with a sleep-then-assert pattern that cannot see the shape the registry and source-edit arms have, a wait for one presence followed by an assertion about a different absence with no window of its own, so those two crates are not cleared and the corrected walk is next-line work, not built now.
